name: AAA-looking browser environments by measurement (rewind, @rewind02)
good_for: 3d game-graphics pbr lookdev color-grading reference-matching ai-workflow
description: X post with a 22-second video of a game environment rendered in the browser with Three.js, whose look comes from a physically based rendering pipeline tuned by measurement rather than from image generation. Eight steps: have the model build a PBR pipeline from papers, talks and Unreal's published techniques; add an FFT ocean, physical atmosphere, global illumination and volumetric clouds; add GTAO, volumetric fog, auto exposure and local tone mapping; hand-pick about a dozen reference frames from real games or film for weather, time of day and composition; choose 7-8 sample areas per reference (sunlit grass, shaded grass, sky near the sun, distant water); measure brightness, chroma and hue in those areas and the same areas of the render; least-squares fit across 100+ points for the lowest-error parameters; render, measure and adjust until the numbers match. Its rule: don't ask the AI for a better-looking scene, give it physics to render and numbers to hit
notes: Free to read on X. Post dated 2026-11-20, quoting the same author's earlier post on building a city in Unreal Engine from free Fab assets. The URL is the author's profile because the post's own link was not recorded. A reply notes that badly chosen references waste the measurements

name: 3D ultra-realistic water (MengTo/skills)
good_for: water ocean creek waves reflections foam wake shaders 3d
description: Agent skill for realistic water in Three.js. Main module: an open ocean from an 8-wave deep-water Gerstner spectrum shaded per pixel from analytic derivatives, with each wave faded once its wavelength drops below the pixel footprint (which stops the far sea boiling into moire), Fresnel reflections from a sky cube plus a half-resolution planar pass, subsurface light through the crests, HDR sun glitter left for the bloom, Jacobian lace foam, a Kelvin wake, hull foam, buoyancy height queries from the same spectrum, and fog into the sky's own horizon haze. Gives the constants that shipped, eight rules each with the failure it prevents, cost figures and a verification checklist. A second recipe covers a shallow creek: flow deflected round rocks, the bed refracted from scene depth with per-channel absorption, a clipped planar reflection weighted by Fresnel, and cascades placed from lip velocity and drop. Ships ocean.mjs (takes the project's own THREE), creek-optics.mjs, check scripts and a runnable demo
notes: MIT (repo LICENSE). One skill folder inside MengTo/skills (listed separately): copy the folder into your skills directory or point the agent at its SKILL.md; no install command. Extracted from Pirate Ship Sunset (Three.js r169). Expects linear HDR into a half-float target with ACES applied once in the composite. Ocean mesh is 167,600 triangles; the skill says to use something cheaper for mirror-flat water, cursor ripples or a small touch pool. The creek recipe is prose plus small helpers, not a drop-in module. Read against a narrow canal: the ocean module does not fit, and the creek recipe's depth-refracted bed adds little when the bed is flat and drawn in the water shader; its sibling 3d-harbour-water suited a canal better

name: raea (Render Anything Engine)

description: Render engine built for AI agents: you tell your agent (Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi or a local model) what to make and it writes videos, motion graphics, 3D and games as React and TypeScript compositions, which raea renders on your own GPU faster than they play. name: bide
good_for: audio voice-synthesis singing procedural-audio music npr pencil-shading hand-drawn animation film generative single-file
description: A 2 min 32 s music film in one HTML file: Danny Boy sung by a voice written in plain Python and drawn by hand in code. The voice is a simulated vocal tract (glottis, throat, mouth, nose and lips moved by jaw, tongue, lips and velum); a performance layer adds glides, breaths, late per-word vibrato and rubato; the band (plucked harp, bowed strings, low whistle, far pipes) is modelled too, mixed in a stone-room reverb and encoded with its own FLAC encoder. The film is a WebGL2 engine that repaints every frame as pastel, pencil and graphite on toothy paper at 12 drawings a second, with poseable drawings of a mother and son, glens, weather and a cottage, in 19 shots timed to the sung words with handwritten lyrics. No text-to-speech, samples, recordings, ML models, fonts, images or CDN; the page makes no network request
notes: MIT (repo LICENSE). Python 3.13 standard library only and plain JavaScript; ./make.sh renders the voice, band and mix and writes dist/bide.html, every random choice seeded; each stage also runs on its own (music/perform.py, voice/sing.py, band/render.py, mix/mix.py, mix/flac.py, tools/build.py). film/dev.html opens the film without sound; tools/shot.mjs and tools/record.mjs (Node, Chrome, macOS) capture stills and video. Worth reading for the code, not as a library: voice/ (tube model, gestures, glottis), band/, mix/flac.py and film/engine.js (the paper and pencil repaint). Made with Claude Opus 5.5 and subagents per its README. Very new (first pushed 2026-11-24, a handful of stars)
